title: U.S. House · Illinois's 4th District
area: Parts of Chicago's West and Southwest Sides and western Cook County suburbs

context.text: This is an open seat. Incumbent Jesus "Chuy" Garcia (D) withdrew from the Democratic primary in November 2025, after the candidate filing deadline, citing health and family reasons. Patty Garcia, who served as his district director and chief of staff, was the only other candidate who had filed and won the Democratic primary unopposed. Lupe Castillo won the Republican primary and Ed Hershey won the Working Class Party primary, both unopposed.
Chris Getty, Mayor of Lyons and Lyons Township Supervisor, is running as an independent after collecting signatures to appear on the general-election ballot.

candidates.name: Patty Garcia
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed

priorities.text: Campaign website says she has built coalitions "standing with immigrant families facing detention and deportation, helping tenants and homeowners navigate rising costs and displacement, and working with labor and community partners."
On affordability, says she would work on raising the federal minimum wage, passing the PRO Act, expanding the Child Tax Credit, reducing prescription drug costs, and building more affordable homes.

On immigration, her campaign website says she supports a pathway to citizenship, protections for Dreamers and mixed-status families, and restructuring immigration enforcement agencies, including abolishing ICE.

positions.summary: Says she would work to raise the federal minimum wage.
Supports a pathway to citizenship and restructuring immigration enforcement agencies, including abolishing ICE, rather than expanding enforcement.
positions.quote: supports a pathway to citizenship, protections for Dreamers and mixed-status families, expanded legal services for immigrants, and stronger oversight and accountability for federal immigration agencies. She also supports fundamentally restructuring immigration enforcement agencies, including abolishing ICE.

positions.summary: Her campaign issues page says she backs Medicare for All.
positions.quote: Patty backs Medicare for All to ensure healthcare as a human right

positions.summary: Her campaign issues page says she is advocating for making the rich pay their due share.
positions.quote: making the rich pay their due share

positions.summary: Her campaign issues page says she favors expanding clean energy and moving toward a clean energy economy.
positions.quote: finally moving towards a clean energy economy

positions.summary: Her campaign issues page says she favors more congressional control over the use of military force.
positions.quote: Patty favors more congressional control over the use of military force

positions.summary: Her campaign issues page calls for ending all U.S. military assistance and arms shipments to Israel in its attack on Gaza.
positions.quote: cessation of all United States military assistance and arms shipments to Israel in its attack on Gaza

candidates.name: Lupe Castillo
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 17, 2026 Republican primary unopposed

priorities.text: Lists no tax on tips and overtime as a campaign priority.
priorities.quote: I am the Only Candidate who supports NO TAX ON TIPS AND OVERTIME, in order to help working class families.

priorities.text: Lists directing federal funds to needy Americans rather than NGOs as a campaign priority.
priorities.quote: I am the Only Candidate who supports government funds going directly to needy Americans instead of politically corrupt NGOs.

priorities.text: Lists a pay halt for members of Congress during government shutdowns as a campaign priority.
priorities.quote: I am the Only Candidate who supports no congressional pay during government shutdowns.

statements.quote: I am the Only Candidate who supports school choice for poor families.
I am the Only Candidate that will protect women's sports and girl's bathrooms.

candidates.name: Ed Hershey
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 17, 2026 Working Class Party primary unopposed

priorities.text: Says the working class needs its own party and organization.
priorities.quote: To say that the working class needs its own party, its own organization.

priorities.text: Names inflation and high prices for food, rent and utilities as the most pressing issue.
priorities.quote: Inflation and high prices for things like food, rent and utilities.

priorities.text: Says he opposes what he calls a push toward war and immigration enforcement by militarized police forces.
priorities.quote: To call out the push towards war that we see in this country

positions.summary: Says corporations and the wealthy should bear the tax burden.
positions.quote: Corporations and the wealthy -- those that have money -- should bear the burden of taxes in this society.

positions.summary: Says a public health system would be a start toward addressing rising costs.
positions.quote: Having a public system, rather than a system designed to shovel our money at the big insurance companies, would be a start.

positions.summary: Describes immigration enforcement by ICE and the Border Patrol as an invasion of streets by militarized police forces and says everyone living and working in the country should have full rights.
positions.quote: the invasion of our streets by militarized police forces like ICE and the Border Patrol

candidates.name: Chris Getty
candidates.currentRole: Mayor of Lyons, Illinois (since 2009); Lyons Township Supervisor (since 2017)

priorities.text: Campaign focuses on cost of living, immigration and public safety, and government accountability, per his campaign website.
"I'm running as an independent because this moment demands an independent voice. I don't answer to a party, I answer to the people."
Says his time as mayor "focused on responsible leadership, economic development, and building partnerships that create real opportunity for residents and local businesses."

record.text: As Mayor of Lyons, oversaw local economic development initiatives, according to his campaign materials.

researchNotes: Garcia's and Getty's material is drawn from their campaign websites as compiled by Ballotpedia. Lupe Castillo's statements come from the values page of her campaign website; no Ballotpedia survey or debate transcript with her own quotes was found. Ed Hershey's positions and priorities come from his WTTW 2026 voter-guide Q&A; no campaign website of his own was found. Garcia's and Getty's material is drawn from their campaign websites as compiled by Ballotpedia, the Sun-Times and WGN; Garcia's earlier career and degree dates come from BallotReady, and her own campaign website could not be loaded. Castillo's and Hershey's biographies come from Ballotpedia (including their 2024 Candidate Connection surveys) and the Sun-Times; no 2026 campaign website or survey was found for them, and their entries are marked minimal. Sources differ on Hershey's years at Lindblom (18 in his 2024 survey, 16 in a 2026 Sun-Times report), so the figure is omitted.
